summary.problem: The security policy engine is bypassed for file-editing tools (such as replace) when the target file is open in the IDE editor context.
summary.root_cause: Tool validation or path evaluation in PolicyEngine/Scheduler does not consistently enforce policy rules when files are active or open in the IDE context.
summary.context: Active IDE editor context provides open file metadata, but policy enforcement must remain strictly uniform across CLI and IDE interactive modes.

steps: Inspect PolicyEngine evaluation logic in packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts to ensure argsPattern and file path matching apply consistently regardless of IDE open file context.
Ensure checkPolicy in packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.ts enforces DENY decisions prior to tool invocation or IDE diff prompts.
Verify that active IDE context state does not bypass PolicyEngine validation during tool scheduling in packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Policy rules with decision 'deny' for file modification tools are strictly enforced whether or not the file is open in the IDE context.
verification_steps: Add unit test cases in packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts with deny policy rules matching file patterns.
Assert that PolicyEngine checks deny file editing tool calls targeting protected files in all IDE context states.

github_metadata.title: Policy is bypassed if the file is opened in the IDE
